cases.name: good_green_increase
cases.description: Green athlete, increase action, volume +7%, 2x frequency, grounded notes
issues_found: Monday's RPE targets are slightly above the recommended range for accumulation phases.
Thursday's RPE targets are slightly above the recommended range for accumulation phases.
Friday's RPE targets are slightly above the recommended range for accumulation phases.
The plan does not include any direct arm work, which is typically beneficial for hypertrophy goals.

cases.name: good_red_deload
cases.description: Red athlete, deload action, volume 60% of baseline, RPE ~6, 4 rest days
issues_found: Volume reduction is only 40%, not the recommended 40-50%.
Intensity reduction is not clearly over 20% for all exercises.
Rep ranges for strength are not fully aligned with typical strength training protocols.
The plan does not explicitly state adherence to the deload protocol for overreaching.

cases.name: good_amber_maintain
cases.description: Amber athlete, maintain action, volume ~99% of baseline, RPE <= 8
issues_found: The plan does not explicitly address the fatigue level 'amber' with specific recovery strategies beyond maintaining volume and avoiding intensity increases.
The plan lacks mention of monitoring or adjustments for worsening fatigue.
The plan's notes about maintaining volume and avoiding intensity increases are supported, but there is no mention of monitoring fatigue signs.
The exercise selection and rep ranges are generally appropriate for strength goals, but the plan could benefit from more variety in exercises.

cases.name: good_fresh_start
cases.description: No-history beginner, conservative starter plan at RPE 6
issues_found: Monday and Wednesday both include Goblet Squats, potentially overloading quads and glutes without sufficient recovery.
The plan does not clearly differentiate between exercises for progression and those for maintenance.
The plan's notes suggest adding 2.5kg next week, but this is not aligned with the 'maintain' progression decision.
The plan does not specify how it will adjust if the athlete cannot complete all sets at the prescribed RPE.
The use of RPE 6 is supported for establishing a baseline, but the plan does not explain how it will transition to higher intensities.

cases.name: good_swap_honoured
issues_found: Saturday session repeats Wednesday's exercises without adequate recovery time.
Friday's session focuses on machine-based lower body exercises, which may not align with the strength goal as effectively as free weights.
The plan does not explicitly address the recommendation to avoid intensity increases given the amber fatigue level.
The plan does not incorporate additional rest days or extended recovery windows despite the amber fatigue level.

cases.name: good_endurance_mix
cases.description: Endurance athlete: run quality + long run + 2 strength support days
issues_found: Monday's cardio session at RPE 8 may be too intense for an endurance block focused on sustainable volume increases.
Thursday's tempo run at RPE 7.5 is close to the upper limit for early training blocks, which should target RPE 6-7.
The plan does not clearly align strength exercises with the goal of improving running economy.
The plan lacks specific evidence or rationale for the selection of strength exercises in relation to endurance goals.

cases.name: bad_consecutive_heavy
cases.description: Same heavy lower-body session on consecutive days
violations: SAFETY: monday and tuesday both load ['glutes', 'hamstrings', 'quads'] above RPE 7.0 — consecutive heavy sessions for the same muscle group.
issues_found: Consecutive heavy lower body sessions on Monday and Tuesday violate recovery guidelines.
Back-to-back heavy lower sessions are not supported for hypertrophy; recovery is insufficient.
The plan does not utilize undulating periodization, which is more effective for intermediates.
The rep range for hypertrophy is not consistently applied; Monday and Tuesday use strength-oriented rep ranges.
The plan's overall notes claim back-to-back heavy sessions maximize stimulus, which is unsupported.

cases.name: bad_deload_no_reduction
cases.description: Deload action but planned volume ~= baseline
violations: COHERENCE: action is deload but planned volume is 7397kg = 99% of the 7500kg weekly baseline (must be <= 85%).
issues_found: Volume deload not achieved: planned volume is 99% of baseline, should be <= 85%.
Intensity reduction insufficient: compound lift intensity not reduced by at least 20% as recommended.
Insufficient rest days: only 3 rest days planned, should be at least 2 full rest days.
Rep ranges for strength not fully aligned: some exercises use higher reps than typical for strength focus.
Groundedness issue: plan notes do not cite specific evidence for deload protocol or rep ranges.

cases.name: bad_increase_decrease
cases.description: Increase action but planned volume is 80% of baseline
violations: COHERENCE: action is increase but planned volume is 7197kg = 80% of baseline — no actual increase.
issues_found: Volume decrease instead of increase despite progression decision to increase.
Hypertrophy goal not fully supported by exercise selection and rep ranges.
RPE targets are appropriate for fatigue level but not aligned with hypertrophy goal.
Insufficient frequency for hypertrophy as major muscle groups are not trained 2x per week.

cases.name: bad_ungrounded_claims
cases.description: Plan notes cite claims the knowledge base contradicts (25-30% jumps, no deloads needed)
issues_found: Monday and Thursday have the same upper body exercises, potentially insufficient recovery.
Tuesday and Friday have the same lower body exercises, potentially insufficient recovery.
The plan claims 25-30% weekly volume increases are standard for intermediates, which is unsupported.
The plan claims deloads are unnecessary for athletes under 30, which is unsupported.
The plan does not align with the hypertrophy goal as it lacks sufficient volume increase and variety.

cases.name: bad_wrong_goal_reps
cases.description: Endurance goal but the plan is pure heavy triples with zero conditioning
issues_found: Monday, Wednesday, and Friday sessions focus on heavy triples, which is not aligned with endurance goals.
RPE targets are too high for an endurance-focused block, especially with heavy triples.
No endurance-specific training sessions are included in the plan.
The plan's overall notes claim an endurance development block, but the exercises and rep ranges do not support this.

cases.name: bad_deload_max_intensity
cases.description: Deload with correct volume cut but RPE 9 grinding on every lift
issues_found: Monday: Near-maximal effort (RPE 9) is inappropriate for a deload week.
Wednesday: Heavy doubles (RPE 9) contradicts deload principles.
Friday: Grinding pulls (RPE 9) are too intense for a deload.
Overall: The plan does not reduce intensity sufficiently for a deload.

issues_found: Seven consecutive training days without rest violates recovery principles.
Back-to-back upper body sessions (Monday, Wednesday, Friday) without adequate recovery.
